Source & methodology · Example report

ETHEREUM MAINNET · USDT

USDT investigation workspace

Review an Ethereum address, inspect its USDT transfers, and document your assessment. Start with the saved example or collect a new bounded case.

1. Define your review

Maximum 2 hours, 700 blocks, 1,000 events. End at least 20 minutes ago for finalized data. Queries send the address to the public node at rpc.mevblocker.io. Historical access and availability may be limited.

Loading saved case…

2. Inspect the activity

Arrows show recorded sender → recipient. Click a node to filter transfers. Gold is the subject address, green is a direct counterparty, and purple is an indirect counterparty. Relationships do not establish identical funds or common ownership.

Case scope & findings

An address is not a person. Activity patterns alone do not establish wrongdoing, common control, or USD conversion inside an exchange.

Candidate sequences

Equal positive amounts recorded sequentially through an intermediary within 30 minutes, up to 20 pairs. These are leads, not proven funds flows. Click to filter that intermediary.

Transfer evidence

UTC / blockSenderRecipientUSDTTransaction / log
Select a transaction for full evidence details.

3. Record your assessment

Notes stay in this tab and are not sent to the node or saved to a server. Export before closing or refreshing. Switching cases preserves notes only while this tab remains open.

Provenance & limits

New queries retain raw node requests and responses in the evidence export. The saved example’s raw evidence is in GitHub under data/raw. Block hashes are checked against node responses; saved-case checksums are verified at build time. Neither check is cryptographic proof of inclusion. Provider completeness is assumed. An event sender is not necessarily the transaction signer. Opening balances, KYC and exchange fiat-conversion records are not available here.
